## Design

### 2026-11-05: I started work on the schematic for the device, reading up on datasheets and figuring out the particular RF purposes for the different components

**2.62h**

I started work on the schematic for the device, reading up on datasheets and figuring out the particular RF purposes for the different components

I decided against the dc-dc converter and for the LDO on the sx1262 since I'll likely just have powered wired directly through usb, and it requires more consideration on particular routing.  The added complexity for a little extra efficiency seemed a bit above my skill level

I put 3 MCUs on the schematic file since I was still a little unsure on which one I wanted to use

### 2026-11-06: Looking back on what the progress I made before, maybe choosing footprints that make the copper pads EXTRA thick isn't that great for all the high frequency work that the board is meant to deal with..

**2.52h**

Looking back on what the progress I made before, maybe choosing footprints that make the copper pads EXTRA thick isn't that great for all the high frequency work that the board is meant to deal with...

Finding out that there exists RF components / ICs that do a lot of the heavy lifting really lifted my spirits after seeing what the actual internals are supposed to do. In fact according to Michael Ossmann its reccomended to use the most integrated components, so I'll listen to someone who has a clue as to what they're doing.

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 072121](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Xt10ZK7FTi1vKiU37U67a1QQj2rKZWIn/7d3c0d363cb701a4b1de12e8c2c6f938ec54ea9bcc653c6ac7339824c19fe671.png)

I think I'm set on using the ESP32-C3 that I have, and I'm not sure how well it is configured for this type of TF project, but considering it has decent range on its wifi I'll hope that there's a ferrite bead or something that keeps it optimized.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/9c844c3a-4869-44b3-ba30-2fc1ec20171d/video.mp4)

### 2026-11-06: From last time I have routed the PCB and rotated the LoRa module to be as accessible as possible. I've learned about via fencing to encapsulate some of the RF stuff,

**2.87h**

From last time I have routed the PCB and rotated the LoRa module to be as accessible as possible. I've learned about via fencing to encapsulate some of the RF stuff,
I'm thinking of including an oled screen next to the esp32 for added information about connecting things, right now it is just headers on the edge of the board, and they can be connected if desired

### 2026-11-08: Got to looking at firmware and the actual availability of the components I want to use.

**4.37h**

Got to looking at firmware and the actual availability of the components I want to use.
I found out the LCSC has a shortage on the filter I wanted to use so I have to redesign the board with its discrete parts.
I converted a lot of the 0402 footprint components to 0603 since it would be cheaper from JLCPCB's assembly

I'm trying to create a new variant that meshcore can support for this project
I copied the repository from their github and updated it to my needs, but I think there is still work to do for makign it work properly with the PlatformIO toolchain

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/4cd9905d-4abc-455a-b229-4fad3a4fd74c/video.mp4)

### 2026-11-08: I started cleaning up the PCB form all the silkscreen designators and the values since they were cluttering the limited amount of space that I had available.

**5.53h**

I started cleaning up the PCB form all the silkscreen designators and the values since they were cluttering the limited amount of space that I had available.

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 184657](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Xt10ZK7FTi1vKiU37U67a1QQj2rKZWIn/1f4bae5a800ccb8eeb20eb8e44dd50d4c6af9d65d8c8873665c1b8768915d203.png)
I finally got the firmware to actually build, now whether it will work with real hardware, who knows.

I designed a simple small enclosure, which I'm hoping can keep the dust out. I opened up a spot for the antenna to go through, and allowed a little overhang on the top so the oled screen could have a bit of support and isn't solely dependent on the solder joints for stability.
